note: Pass with substantial caveats -- three of them, and the first is a correction to the deposit. (1) THE DEPOSIT README MISDESCRIBES THIS BLOCK. The Dryad README (doi:10.5061/dryad.brv15dvkd) says 'YDCY: Godin Leisure Time Exercise Questionnaire, GLTEQ. YDCY1-YDCY5 represents questions one to five in the scale' and then prints GLTEQ wording -- vigorous/moderate/light weekly frequency counts for questions 2, 3 and 4, and the GLTEQ weighting rule 'Multiply the answer to question two by 9, the answer to question three by 5, and the answer to question four by 3'. That is false of the data. The .sav's own composite column YDCY equals YDCY2*YDCY3*YDCY4 exactly for 879/879 respondents (max|diff| 0, range 0-100), while the README's GLTEQ weighting reproduces 5/879 (max|diff| 60). The product form is the PARS-3 formula the PLOS article states in Instruments section (4): 'Physical Exercise Volume = Intensity x (Duration-1) x Frequency', with the article's own 0-100 banding (low <=19, moderate 20-42, high >=43) matching the observed composite range exactly. So YDCY2-YDCY4 are PARS-3, not GLTEQ, and the README's numbered sentences for questions 2-4 were NOT shipped. Step 3b outcome: the table name and dictionary Description are right (physical activity rating), the deposit README is the thing that is wrong. (2) WHICH PARS-3 DIMENSION IS WHICH -- one item pinned by the data, two by canonical order. PARS-3 stores duration as (level-1), so duration alone can be 0 while intensity and frequency run 1-5. YDCY3 is the only one of the three carrying zeros (58 of 879, range 0-4); YDCY2 and YDCY4 are 1-5 with no zeros. That identifies YDCY3 as duration outright. It does NOT separate intensity from frequency: the composite is a product and so is symmetric in YDCY2 and YDCY4, both are 1-5, and no test on this data distinguishes them. YDCY2=intensity and YDCY4=frequency rest on the canonical PARS-3 presentation order (intensity, duration, frequency), corroborated only by the uniquely identifiable duration item landing in the middle position. Verification status is PARTIAL for that reason, and a YDCY2/YDCY4 swap would leave every number in verify_liu_2025_ydcy.R unchanged. (3) A RESPONSE-DATA DEFECT WORTH FIXING UPSTREAM. data/liu_2025_teacher_support.py drops YDCY3's 58 zero responses on the reasoning that zeros 'isolated to that single item with no 0s anywhere else in the YDCY block' are the cross-item data-entry-error signature. They are not an error: 0 is PARS-3's lowest valid duration score, i.e. the 'Under 10 minutes' option, which by construction can only appear on the duration item. Those 58 respondents are exactly the ones whose composite YDCY is 0 (n=58, the lowest exercise-volume band). The live table therefore has YDCY3 n=821 against 879 for the other items, and its lowest surviving level (resp 1) means '11 to 20 minutes', not the bottom of the scale. Nothing here is fixable from the item-text side -- flagged for the response-data owner. No option row is shipped for resp 0 because that value is not in the live table. (4) ADMINISTERED IN CHINESE, SHIPPED IN ENGLISH, FROM TWO DIFFERENT ENGLISH SOURCES. 879 middle-school students in Kaifeng surveyed on site, so the administered wording was Chinese; no Chinese wording is recoverable in scope (the deposit is exactly PLOSONE.sav + README.md, the .sav carries ZERO variable labels and ZERO value labels across all 74 columns -- checked -- and the README is English throughout; the article has only S1 File, which is that .sav). The 2026-09-01 fallback applies: English in the base fields, language=Chinese, the four _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute. translation_source=mixed because the two halves came from different places -- YDCY2/3/4 stems and all fifteen option anchors are transcribed verbatim from a CC BY Frontiers supplementary that prints the whole PARS-3 form in English (Chen, Liu, Mou, Zhao & Guo 2022, Front Psychol 13:964169, Supplementary Data Sheet 1), and YDCY5 is verbatim from this study's own Dryad README. (5) YDCY5 OPTION DIRECTION was settled from the data because the README contradicts itself: its question 1 numbers the same sweat-frequency item '(1) Never/Rarely, (2) Sometimes, (3) Often' while its question 5 lists it '1 Often 2 Sometimes 3 Never/Rarely'. YDCY5 correlates +0.273 with the exercise-volume composite and +0.222/+0.176/+0.216 with the three PARS-3 items, so a higher code means more exercise: 1=Never/Rarely, 2=Sometimes, 3=Often, the question-1 numbering. Distribution 88/525/266. (6) MINOR. instructions and section_prompt blank -- neither the article nor the README publishes any; single trivial section_id; correct_response empty (no correct answer), so key_source empty. The Frontiers form's stem wording was transcribed character for character including 'e.g.' and 'etc.'; only the leading item numbering and the option bullets were stripped. RIGHTS: nothing to quote. PARS-3 (Hashimoto 1990, revised by Liang Deqing 1994) carries no findable fee, non-commercial clause or redistribution bar, and both pages the words were copied from are open (Frontiers CC BY; the Dryad README beside a CC BY 4.0 PLOS article). The one English rendering found under CC BY-NC-ND (Jiang 2025, BMC Psychol 13:54, PMC11748591) was deliberately NOT used, per the source-licence rule. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped. Every in-scope source (article, PLOS S1 .sav, Dryad record and README) was fetched and read, and the residual uncertainty (YDCY2 vs YDCY4) is a property of the data, not an access failure: an unchanged retry now would reproduce this exactly.

BLOCKED on a rights clause quoted from the instrument's own rights holder. The table is the mudfold R package's `Loneliness` dataset (11 items A-K, resp 1-3), i.e. the De Jong Gierveld 11-item Loneliness Scale; the dictionary DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/U6GCK is the authors' own manual. Extraction was fully solvable -- mudfold's Loneliness.Rd documents each column A-K against its statement verbatim ('A': 'There is always someone I can talk to about my day to day problems (+)' ... 'K': 'I can call on my friends whenever I need them (+)'), the .RData columns carry embedded value labels (-1 'no answer', 1 'no', 2 'more-or-less', 3 'yes'), and data/mudfold.R takes `item` straight from colnames() with no rename, so mapping would have been data_labels with no inference. Nothing was shipped because the rights holder's manual (de Jong Gierveld & van Tilburg, Manual for the Loneliness Scale, 2026 update, osf.io/u6gck, p.1) states use conditions on the scale materials including: 'Not commercial - You may not use the material for commercial purposes.' and 'No derivatives - If you remix, transform or build upon the material, you may not distribute the modified material.' The 1999 edition IRW's dictionary cites is likewise conditional: 'The scale is available for scientific research programs, under the following conditions:' followed by a requirement that manuscripts and part of the research data be sent to the authors. A stated non-commercial restriction on the wording is the exact trigger in references/itemtext_standard.md ('If the wording's rights holder states a non-commercial restriction on the item text, do not ship it'), and the 2026-09-05 HEXACO ruling plus the 2026-09-06 retirement of wording_rights mean a stated use restriction now blocks outright rather than being flagged and shipped. That IRW's copy would have come from the GPL-2 mudfold package does not save it: the DSES ruling (2026-09-04) settled that a rights holder's own restriction outranks the deposit's licence. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: this is an instrument-level ruling, not a table-level one -- any other IRW table carrying De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale wording is in the same position and should be checked. No verification_/verify_ sidecar is written: SKILL Step 5b states a blocked table has no live item text and so cannot carry a verification outcome of any kind. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict (licence bars reuse). The wording was located, transcribed-ready and mappable; only a ruling from Ben that this NC/ND clause does not block, or a change in the rights holder's stated terms, would change the outcome. An unchanged retry now would reach the same block.
